1.bug_scenario: In the CodePen capture we see a T-SQL block where a dynamically generated SQL string uses nested single-quote escape sequences at the very end (for example: N''DROP VIEW IF EXISTS ...;'';). The built-in SQL grammar in highlight.js (loaded by calling highlight on a <code class="sql"> block) fails to correctly match the closing quotes on that line, causing the remainder of the script to be mis-highlighted.

2.explanation: The only place in highlight.js that governs SQL string highlighting is the default export in sql.js. Inside that function there is a ‘string’ mode defined with begin: '\'' and end: '\'' and a single escape rule contains: [{ begin: "''" }]. This rule handles two single quotes in a row but does not account for prefixed Unicode string literals (the N''…'' syntax) or nested escapes at the very start/end of the string. As a result the opening and closing quotes around the inner DROP VIEW command (N''…'';) confuse the mode and break out of the intended string matching.
2.bug_scenario: The user is writing dynamic T-SQL that embeds a nested, doubled‐quote escape sequence (the N''DROP VIEW IF EXISTS ...''; snippet) inside a single‐quoted string. In the CodePen screenshot you can see the SQL code begins parsing correctly but after the nested N''…'' escape sequence the highlighter never recovers, coloring everything as a string or otherwise misformatting the rest of the block.
